questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: How mythology has shaped cultural traditions.
options.B: Joseph Campbell's influence on storytelling techniques.
options.C: The structure and significance of the hero's journey.

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make about Joseph Campbell?

options.A: He invented the hero's journey as a new storytelling model.
options.B: He examined why readers are drawn to heroic actions in stories.
options.C: He was best known for writing fiction based on ancient stories.
options.D: He found that stories from different cultures share a similar pattern.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention a gift?

options.A: To show appreciation for storytellers' creative talents.
options.B: To point out what makes the hero's journey meaningful.
options.C: To describe what the hero receives from a mentor.
options.D: To highlight the hero's motivation for starting the journey.

questions.stem: What is the speaker's opinion about the hero's journey in storytelling?

options.A: It is outdated and no longer relevant.
options.B: It limits creativity by focusing only on action and adventure.
options.C: It is influential because it reflects shared human experiences.
options.D: It has become more popular due to its use in film and media.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?

options.A: The importance of brand reputation for the brand's success.
options.B: A new method by which brands gain attention.
options.C: The marketing of a drug for a virus.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the cost of viral marketing?

options.A: It is cost-effective compared to traditional advertising methods.
options.B: It is more expensive than other forms of advertising.
options.C: It involves higher costs at first but lower costs later.

options.B: It is usually produced by young people.
